chapter: Buddy Petit and brass band reading
title: Listening to a record for Buddy Petit's style
summary: While a record plays they debate whether it is Buddy Petit or an imitator; Ridgley says people loved Buddy despite his bad habits.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: That's his style. What does it sound like?
That's funny. It ain't somebody just like you, but that's his style. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. That's just like him. Somebody show him and then imitate him.
Somebody imitate him is what I figured.
I hear that that's his style and I wanted you to tell me because I know you'd know.

That's his style. You know who played on his order? Who's that? The white boy got the band. What's his name now? Old, old, old musician. He'd be playing, making good money later. That's his name now. That's his name now. That's his name now. . You like Sash playing Star Ben South Stand?
But South Stand knew how to get along with the people, huh? I haven't think much of his playing.
No. He just had a good wonderful name. Mutt. Sash. Sash is good. Sweet. That's his star. If it ain't him, it's somebody much just like him.

That's every bit of his star. He was good. People used to ask for him all the time, but he just had that bad habit, you know. I understand he's such a nice fellow. People didn't like him. But Mutt and that boy, they'd ask for him all the time.
Oh, yeah. Yeah, that's interesting to hear that that really liked Buddy, huh?
Just liked him. He could just, he's now trombone player with Buddy, Buddy, he's learning how to make all of his part, and he could help everybody out in the band. He's just gifted.
